A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–I. The pagination difference reflects reflow, with no missing scientific material.

before.justification: v1 reports original unlearning experiments on LLaMA and Qwen, calibration results, and comparisons between LLM and human judges in Section 6, with additional empirical results in Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original unlearning, calibration, and human-evaluation results in Section 6 and Appendices D–F.

M1.justification: The supporting-subgraph extraction, confidence calibration and filtering, and adversarial LLM-judge procedures are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the prompts in Appendix C are retained identically.

E1.justification: Both versions use YAGO3-10 for relational-knowledge unlearning and MMLU and BBH for utility evaluation. No datasets, tasks, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 and corresponding analyses retain GA, RL, NPO, NegGrad+, and SCRUB, with the same no-unlearning reference. The comparison between instance-level and supporting-subgraph evaluation also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the same 200 target triples, 2,000 neighboring utility triples, validation samples, model configurations, sentence/QA formats, metrics, and judge procedures. Reported training budgets and epoch-selection rules are unchanged in Section 6.1 and Appendix B.

E4.justification: The entropy-threshold, forget-set-size, epoch, calibration, local-consistency, and score-distribution analyses are unchanged. The judge-discrepancy examples and residual-inferability case studies in Appendix E are also retained.

E5.justification: Both disclose random seed 42 in Appendix D.2 and three LLM scoring rounds plus three independent human ratings for 50 supporting subgraphs in Section 6.3. Repeated-evaluation and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains LLaMA QA-LoRA NPO UES values of 0.690 for instance evaluation and 0.585 for the proposed evaluation; Figure 7 retains Pearson correlation 0.826.

T1.justification: Definition 1, the graph and judge formulations, metric equations, Appendix B objectives, and Appendix G entropy-to-probability derivation are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or mathematical results are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: confidence-aware correlated knowledge enables residual inference, and conventional evaluations can overestimate unlearning effectiveness.

C2.justification: Interpretations of utility trade-offs, low-confidence supporting facts, and judge disagreements remain unchanged. Appendix I retains the same scientific limitations concerning evaluator strength, incomplete subgraphs, inaccurate probing, and reference-graph coverage.

D1.justification: The code-access statement and repository address are unchanged. Appendices B–D retain identical hyperparameters, prompts, hardware and software descriptions, filtering details, runtime disclosures, and reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 65 references and the same positioning relative to prior unlearning benchmarks, multi-fact evaluation, and knowledge editing. No cited works or substantive novelty comparisons change.

P1.justification: v2 removes Mohsen Ghassemi and Vamsi K. Potluru from the author list and adds them to the acknowledgments. Their affiliation/contact information and the JP Morgan disclaimer are removed; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The shorter author block and removed disclaimer cause minor shifts in text and figure placement and reflow the references. Figures 1–30 and Tables 1–7 retain their content and design; appendix pages are visually identical apart from page numbers.

improvement.justification: v2 revises authorship and acknowledgments, removes institutional legal boilerplate, and slightly reflows the document. The scientific exposition, evidence, limitations, and reproducibility material—including all appendices—remain unchanged, leaving overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
